description: A valid design token system has a primitive foundation, semantic aliases on top, and component tokens that never skip tiers.

rules.description: At least one primitive-tier token must exist. Primitives hold raw values (hex, px, rem) and are the source of truth for all other tiers.
At least one semantic-tier token must exist. Semantics give intent-based names (action-primary, surface-default) to primitive values, enabling theming.

Every token type must be one of the allowed set: color, spacing, sizing, typography, border-radius, border-width, shadow, motion, z-index, opacity, font-family, font-size, font-weight, line-height, letter-spacing, duration, easing.
Every token tier must be one of: primitive, semantic, component. Unknown tiers indicate a taxonomy error.
Primitive tokens must hold raw values, not alias references. An aliased primitive is a tier violation — it means the true primitive is hidden behind indirection.
